judged_text: createEvent falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` when no destinationCalendar entry matches the given credentialId, creating the event on the account's primary calendar with no warning or error. A collective booking where a member's destinationCalendar references a credential that was deleted or belongs to another app gets its event silently written to that member's primary Google calendar instead of the intended one; the operation reports success and the booking reference records the wrong externalCalendarId, so later updates/deletes target the wrong calendar.

A collective booking where a member's destinationCalendar references a credential that was deleted or belongs to another app gets its event silently written to that member's primary Google calendar instead of the intended one; the operation reports success and the booking reference records the wrong externalCalendarId, so later updates/deletes target the wrong calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` now picks `selectedCalendar` via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and then calls `calendar.events.insert({ calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary" ... })`. If no destinationCalendar entry matches the passed `credentialId`, the event is silently created on the Google account’s primary calendar. Meanwhile, `packages/core/EventManager.ts` calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` and `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` returns that `externalId` in the `EventResult`, so the booking/reference can record the intended `externalId` even though Google inserted into `primary`, causing later update/delete to target the wrong calendar. This matches the reported silent mis-write behavior.
